result.markdown: --- title: "dsOMOP — Exercises (MIMIC)" subtitle: "Practise the federated-analysis toolkit on new variables and a new model" format: html: df-print: kable execute: eval: false --- Download the worksheet (.R) Source (.Rmd) View solutions # How to use this sheet Everything you need you **already did once** in the [tutorial](dsomop.html). Each exercise gives you a **code skeleton** with blanks marked `____` and a `# STEP` comment telling you what to do — fill in the blanks, run it, and **check the output**. A collapsed **hint** is there if you get stuck. We stay on the **MIMIC** dataset, but use *new* variables. The [worked solutions](omop_exercises_solution.html) (with real output) are one click away. ::: {.callout-important} ## Reminders - Connect with `profile = "omop"`. - Pooled summaries: pass `scope = "pooled"` and read the `$pooled` slot. - Anchor age with `year = 2024` (this extract's collection year). - **Check the output after every step.** ::: ## Setup (run this first) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(DSI); library(DSOpal); library(dsBaseClient); library(dsOMOPClient) builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder() builder$append(server = "nairobi", url = "https://nairobi.datashield.live", user = "ethiopia", password = "P@ssw0rd", profile = "omop") builder$append(server = "douala", url = "https://douala.datashield.live", user = "ethiopia", password = "P@ssw0rd", profile = "omop") builder$append(server = "dakar", url = "https://dakar.datashield.live", user = "ethiopia", password = "P@ssw0rd", profile = "omop") conns <- DSI::datashield.login(logins = builder$build()) ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop_demo.mimic", symbol = "omop", conns = conns) ``` ::: --- # Exercise 1 — Find a concept yourself You suspect **alcohol abuse** is recorded. Find its `concept_id`, then see how many patients have it. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # STEP 1 — search the Condition domain for "alcohol abuse" to get its concept_id ds.omop.concept.search("____", domain = "Condition", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$pooled # STEP 2 — find it in the pooled condition prevalence (ranked by distinct patients) ds.omop.concept.prevalence("condition_occurrence", metric = "persons", top_n = 15, scope = "pooled", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$pooled ``` ::: **Question:** What is the `concept_id`, and roughly how many patients have it? ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint Search the term `"alcohol"`. You are looking for *Alcohol abuse* (`concept_id = 433753`); read its `n_persons` from the prevalence table. ::: # Exercise 2 — A new numeric variable The tutorial summarised heart rate and creatinine. Do the same for **systolic blood pressure** (`concept_id = 21492239`): get its safe statistics and draw its histogram. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # STEP 1 — disclosure-safe summary (pooled): n, mean, sd, p05-p95 ds.omop.column.stats("measurement", "value_as_number", concept_id = ____, scope = "pooled", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$pooled # STEP 2 — its shape: pull the per-site bins, then draw them h <- ds.omop.value.histogram("measurement", value_col = "value_as_number", concept_id = ____, symbol = "omop", conns = conns) # combine h$per_site (drop NA counts), put midpoints on a common grid, then barplot() ``` ::: **Question:** Is systolic blood pressure roughly symmetric, or skewed like creatinine? ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint Use `concept_id = 21492239` in both calls. For the picture, reuse the tutorial's `draw_hist()` helper (copy it across), e.g. `draw_hist(21492239, nbins = 9, xlab = "Systolic BP (mmHg)", main = "Systolic BP")`. Its mean is ~115 mmHg. ::: # Exercise 3 — A new categorical variable The tutorial counted heart **rhythm**. Explore **marital status** (`concept_id = 40766231`, in the `observation` table): count how often each value occurs. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # STEP — marital status is a CODED value, so it lives in value_as_concept_id. Count it, pooled. ds.omop.value.counts("observation", "____", concept_id = 40766231, scope = "pooled", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$pooled ``` ::: **Question:** What is the most common marital status? ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint The column is `"value_as_concept_id"` (categorical measurements/observations store their code there, not in `value_as_number`). ::: # Exercise 4 — Build your own recipe Build a wide person-level table `D` with: **sex**, **age** (anchored to 2024), the **mean systolic blood pressure**, a **binary alcohol-abuse flag** (the concept from Exercise 1), and a **count of hospital visits**. Then ratify what the server built and summarise it. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # STEP 1 — write the recipe: fill the format of each variable and the age anchor year rec <- omop_recipe( variables = list( omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id", format = "sex_mf", name = "sex"), omop_variable_age(name = "age", year = ____), omop_variable(table = "measurement", concept_id = 21492239, format = "____", name = "systolic_bp"), omop_variable(table = "condition_occurrence", concept_id = 433753, format = "____", name = "alcohol_abuse"), omop_variable(table = "visit_occurrence", format = "count", name = "n_visits") ), output = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide")) # STEP 2 — execute into a server symbol D, then RATIFY it was built as you expected recipe_execute(rec, out = c(study = "D"), symbol = "omop", conns = conns) ds.colnames("D", datasources = conns) ds.dim("D", datasources = conns) # STEP 3 — summarise the systolic_bp column ds.summary("D$systolic_bp", datasources = conns)[[1]][["quantiles & mean"]] ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint `year = 2024`; a *mean* lab value is `format = "mean"`; a yes/no condition flag is `format = "binary"`. `D` should have one row per patient with `person_id, sex, age, systolic_bp, alcohol_abuse, n_visits`. ::: # Exercise 5 — Filter at extraction Re-extract, but keep only **male** patients **aged 60+**, as `DSUB`. Confirm the cohort shrank and that everyone is male. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # STEP — add a filters = list(...) with a sex filter and an age filter rec_sub <- omop_recipe( variables = list( omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id", format = "sex_mf", name = "sex"), omop_variable_age(name = "age", year = 2024), omop_variable(table = "condition_occurrence", concept_id = 433753, format = "binary", name = "alcohol_abuse") ), filters = list( male = omop_filter_sex("____"), older = omop_filter_age(min = ____, year = 2024) ), output = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide")) recipe_execute(rec_sub, out = c(study = "DSUB"), symbol = "omop", conns = conns) ds.dim("DSUB", datasources = conns) as.data.frame(ds.table("DSUB$sex", datasources = conns)$output.list[["TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts"]]) ``` ::: **Question:** How many patients remain, and is every one of them male? ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint `omop_filter_sex("M")` and `omop_filter_age(min = 60, year = 2024)`. Filters can only shrink a population, so the count drops. ::: # Exercise 6 — A model Build a table with **sex**, **age** and a **binary hypertension** flag (`concept_id = 320128`), then fit a logistic regression of hypertension on age and sex. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # STEP 1 — recipe + execute into H rec_h <- omop_recipe( variables = list( omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id", format = "sex_mf", name = "sex"), omop_variable_age(name = "age", year = 2024), omop_variable(table = "condition_occurrence", concept_id = 320128, format = "binary", name = "hypertension") ), output = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide")) recipe_execute(rec_h, out = c(study = "H"), symbol = "omop", conns = conns) # STEP 2 — fit the logistic model: fill in the two predictors fit <- ds.glm(formula = "H$hypertension ~ H$____ + H$____", family = "binomial", datasources = conns) fit$coefficients ``` ::: **Question:** Which predictor is significant (p < 0.05)? Is the direction clinically sensible? ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint The predictors are `H$age` and `H$sex`. Read the `p-value` column; `age` should be the significant one (odds of hypertension rise with age). On ~100 patients, expect wide confidence intervals. ::: # Open challenge Pick **any** condition that interests you (find it with `ds.omop.concept.search`), add it to a recipe as a binary flag, and explore whether it is associated with age or sex. There is no single right answer — the skill is running the workflow correctly and reading the result honestly. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # YOUR CODE HERE ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} DSI::datashield.logout(conns) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note} Not every hypothesis pans out — a non-significant result is still a real finding. Doing the analysis correctly matters more than getting stars next to your coefficients. :::
